As we wrap up our journey through The Sleepwalkers, it’s striking how the world of a hundred years ago can feel so distant, yet somehow, so familiar. This isn’t just a story about kings, generals, and diplomats—it’s about the everyday hopes and worries that drive people in power, and the millions whose lives are touched by their choices. It’s a powerful reminder: history isn’t written by heroes or villains alone, but by ordinary people, each acting out of their own beliefs, doubts, and habits.
So, what can we take with us from this story? First, even the smallest decisions—made in the rush of daily life—can sometimes set off events that change everything. Alliances and promises, even when meant to protect, can turn into traps no one saw coming. Pride and fear, the urge to save face, can cloud anyone’s judgment—especially in a crisis. And most leaders think they’re steering the ship—right up until the moment the waves take control. The warning signs? They’re usually easiest to spot when it’s already too late.
If there’s one thing to hold onto, it’s this: stay humble, and stay vigilant. The world’s always more complicated than it looks, and the future gets shaped by the choices we make when we’re uncertain. It’s tempting to think that disasters only happen to other people, in other times—but the lesson of 1914 is clear. No one’s immune to habit, pride, or fear. So, let’s stay awake. Let’s question, let’s listen, and remember—peace is never something we can just assume. In your own life and in your own community, the choices you make matter. We can’t change the past, but the future? That’s still up to us. Stay alert, stay thoughtful, and never underestimate the power of one decision.
